title: What can you say about biotin in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library supports 3 wordings for biotin; the strongest is "Plays a part in normal energy metabolism" (strong, 1.8-500 µg a day). Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Stops hair loss, or regrows hair".

supported_wordings.wording: Helps maintain healthy hair, skin and nails.
supported_wordings.why: Health Canada and the EU accept it, but ODS says the hair, skin and nail claims rest at best on a few case reports and small studies.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Health Canada: 1.8-500 µg a day for adults. EU (hair and skin only): at least 7.5 µg, 15% of the 50 µg EU reference value (Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011, Annex XIII).

sources.name: Commission Regulation (EU) No 432/2012, list of permitted health claims
NIH ODS fact sheet: Biotin (health professional)

supported_wordings.where_sources_disagree: Health Canada lists healthy hair, nails, mucous membranes and skin, and the EU authorizes normal hair, skin and mucous membranes (not nails). ODS says biotin's hair, skin and nail claims are supported, at best, by only a few case reports and small studies.

supported_wordings.wording: Plays a part in normal energy metabolism.
supported_wordings.why: Health Canada lists a role in metabolizing nutrients, and the EU authorizes normal energy-yielding metabolism.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Health Canada: 1.8-500 µg a day for adults. EU: at least 7.5 µg.

sources.name: Commission Regulation (EU) No 432/2012, list of permitted health claims

supported_wordings.wording: Supports normal function of the nervous system.
supported_wordings.why: Authorized in the EU after EFSA review; Health Canada does not list it.
supported_wordings.dose_details: EU: at least 7.5 µg, 15% of the 50 µg EU reference value. 500 µg is Health Canada's adult maximum.

sources.name: Commission Regulation (EU) No 432/2012, list of permitted health claims

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Stops hair loss, or regrows hair
wordings_to_avoid.why: Hair loss can be a sign of disease; ODS says the evidence for hair claims is weak.

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Treats brittle nails or skin rashes
wordings_to_avoid.why: These are listed by ODS as signs of biotin deficiency; wording about treating them is disease wording.

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition

sources.name: Commission Regulation (EU) No 432/2012, list of permitted health claims
NIH ODS fact sheet: Biotin (health professional)

disclaimer: Not legal advice. This guide shows the wording that published evidence supports at a daily dose, from the sources linked below; it is not a ruling on any claim. Your own product, its form and dose, and your own evidence still need to match the wording you use.
